facts.statement: The dinosaur Arcusaurus was first named by Adam Yates, Matthew Bonnan, and Johann Neveling in 2011.
facts.quote: Arcusaurus was first named by Adam Yates, Matthew Bonnan and Johann Neveling in 2011

facts.statement: The genus name Arcusaurus comes from the Latin word for 'rainbow', referencing the Rainbow Nation.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Latin arcus, "rainbow", a reference to the Rainbow Nation.

facts.statement: The species name honors Lucille Pereira and Fernando Abdala, who discovered the fossils.
facts.quote: The specific epithet honours Lucille Pereira and Fernando Abdala who discovered the fossils.

facts.statement: Arcusaurus lived in South Africa during the Early Jurassic period, specifically the Pliensbachian stage.
facts.quote: Arcusaurus is an extinct genus of sauropodomorph dinosaur from the Early Jurassic (Pliensbachian stage) of South Africa.

facts.statement: Fossils of Arcusaurus were collected in March 2006 from the Spion Kop Heelbo site in Senekal, Free State, South Africa.
facts.quote: Arcusaurus is known from remains collected in March 2006 at the Spion Kop Heelbo site from the upper Elliot Formation in Senekal in Free State.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen of Arcusaurus is a partial skull with the catalog number BP/1/6235.
facts.quote: The holotype (specimen number BP/1/6235) consists of a partial skull.

facts.statement: The discovery of two right nasal bones indicates that at least two individuals of Arcusaurus were present at the fossil site.
facts.quote: two right nasal (skull bone located behind the nostril) were discovered, indicating that at least two individuals must have been present

facts.statement: The fossil specimens of Arcusaurus likely represent juveniles, based on their small size and open bone sutures.
facts.quote: The present individuals probably represented juveniles as indicated by small size and open bone sutures.

facts.statement: Detailed analysis confirmed that the Arcusaurus fossils were not juveniles of the species Aardonyx or Massospondylus.
facts.quote: From detailed features the describers concluded these were not juveniles of either Aardonyx or Massospondylus.

facts.statement: Arcusaurus likely had a relatively deep snout, indicated by the square shape of its premaxilla bone.
facts.quote: The snout was probably relatively deep as in plateosaurians, which is indicated by the square shape of the premaxilla, which formed the tip of the snout.

facts.statement: Arcusaurus had nostrils located near the snout tip and a large, circular eye socket similar to the early dinosaur Eoraptor.
facts.quote: The external naris, the opening for the nostril, was located close to the tip of the snout, and the orbit (eye socket) was proportionally large and circular, similar to that of the early dinosaur Eoraptor.

facts.statement: The premaxilla of Arcusaurus contained four teeth on each side.
facts.quote: The premaxilla contained four teeth on each side.

facts.statement: Two bony shelves projected from the inner side of the Arcusaurus premaxilla, one above the other.
facts.quote: Two bony shelfes projected from the inner side of the premaxilla, one above the other.

facts.statement: The two bony shelves on the Arcusaurus premaxilla are unique features that distinguish the genus from related sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: Both the lower shelf and upper shelf are unique features serving to distinguish the genus from related sauropodomorphs.

facts.statement: The Arcusaurus nasal bone was plate-like with four bony extensions: two directed forward and two directed backward.
facts.quote: The nasal bone was plate-like and had four processes (bony extensions), two directed to the front and two to the rear.

facts.statement: The lower forward process of the Arcusaurus nasal bone was tongue-shaped and wider than the upper process, unlike the triangular shape seen in most related genera.
facts.quote: The lower of these processes was tongue-shaped, rather than triangular as in most related genera, and was wider than the upper process, unlike in plateosaurians.

facts.statement: The Arcusaurus postorbital bone formed the upper rear corner of the eye socket and had three large processes extending forward, downward, and backward.
facts.quote: The postorbital formed the upper rear corner of the orbit, and had three large processes, extending toward the front, bottom, and rear, respectively.

facts.statement: A fourth small process on the Arcusaurus postorbital bone pointed upward and inward to connect with the parietal bone, an orientation unique among dinosaurs.
facts.quote: A fourth, smaller process was directed upwards and inwards, and would have articulated with the parietal, the rearmost bone of the skull roof; the orientation of this process in unique in dinosaurs.

facts.statement: The rear-projecting process of the Arcusaurus postorbital bone had a bifurcated tip rather than tapering, unlike most other basal sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: The third process, projecting towards the rear, was not tapering towards its tip, unlike in most other basal sauropodomorphs; instead, its tip was bifurcated.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic studies classify Arcusaurus as a basal sauropodomorph, sister to Efraasia and more derived sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic study of Arcusaurus found it to be a basal sauropodomorph, placing it as the sister taxon of Efraasia and all of the more derived sauropodomorphs.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Arcusaurus belongs with basal sauropodomorphs, as it possesses unique features of the advanced clade Plateosauria that raise doubts about phylogenetic results.
facts.quote: However, Arcusaurus possesses many features unique to more advanced groups included in the clade Plateosauria, raising doubts about the results of the phylogenetic analysis.

facts.statement: The close relationship between Arcusaurus and the Late Triassic dinosaur Efraasia implies a 35-million-year ghost lineage for sauropodomorphs.
facts.quote: Since Efraasia is known from the Norian stage of the Late Triassic, the close relationship with Arcusaurus implies that there was a 35-million-year ghost lineage of sauropodomorphs stretching from Late Triassic forms to Arcusaurus.

facts.statement: Arcusaurus is classified within the order Saurischia and the suborder Sauropodomorpha.
facts.quote: superordo: Dinosauria ordo: Saurischia subordo: Sauropodomorpha

facts.statement: The time range for Arcusaurus is estimated to be between 201.4 and 192.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Sinemurian (201.4 to 192.9 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Arcusaurus lived approximately 196 million years ago during the Early Jurassic, between the Hettangian and Sinemurian stages, in what is now Africa.
